analysis.title: MPLX LP (MPLX): 3Q26 Recap: Confident Message on Growth, Though Refining Logistics Sale Tempers 2027 Distribution
key_insights: MPLX reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $1,859m, slightly above GSe of $1,844m and FactSet consensus of $1,843m (+1% vs each). Crude & Products beat (product pipeline rates +7% vs GSe, terminal throughput +4% vs GSe and +6% YoY on higher exports), mostly offset by softer Natural Gas & NGL on higher opex including incentive compensation.

Sequential EBITDA was up 5% vs 2Q26 ($1,775m) and up 5% YoY (+7% excluding the Rockies divestiture). The quarter included $77m of incentive compensation expense (+$37m YoY), which management said cut 3Q26 YoY EBITDA growth by about 2%.

MPLX announced a $750m sale of logistics assets tied to sponsor MPC's refinery divestiture (an interest in a crude oil pipeline, storage capacity and three terminals) at about 9x company-forecast 2027 EBITDA. That implies about $83m of EBITDA, or about 1% of GS 2027E EBITDA. The sale is guided to close at year-end 2026 and is not in GS estimates.

Management reiterated 2H26-weighted growth, with 4Q26 EBITDA trending higher sequentially (GS estimates +2% QoQ, with Titan II not yet contributing). It still expects 2027 EBITDA growth above 2026 despite the sale and reiterated a mid-single-digit growth outlook (GSe about 5% EBITDA CAGR 2026-2032).

MPLX lowered its 2027+ distribution growth outlook because of the asset sale, after previously guiding to 12.5%. GS now models about +8.5% DPU growth in 2027 (vs 12.5% prior) and about 4% a year for 2028-2032E, in line with DCF growth, to hold a 1.3x coverage ratio. GS says the lower distribution saves about $750m versus about $500m of EBITDA lost through 2032.

The Northeast processing system ran at 93% utilization after Harmon Creek III (300 MMcf/d processing plus a 40 kb/d de-ethanizer) entered service in August. Utica gathering and processing volumes rose 19%/20% YoY, and Utica processing utilization rose to 89% from 73% in 2Q26.

Management does not expect a negative impact from the recent Northeast upstream consolidation, but noted openness to future commercial discussions on rates given the combined customer's greater scale. There was no update on the Northeast behind-the-meter power opportunity.

MPLX (10% interest) and JV partners reached FID on the Solitude Pipeline System, adding 4.5 Bcf/d of Permian gas egress (Phase I 2H29, Phase II 2030) and lifting MPLX's Permian long-haul capacity interest to about 16 Bcf/d from 11 Bcf/d. Titan II completes by year-end 2026 but adds no meaningful 4Q26 volumes, with a ramp toward 400+ MMcf/d through 2027.

Management plans to redeploy the sale proceeds quickly into organic and inorganic opportunities focused on the Permian and Marcellus, with mid-teens return targets. It says it can reach mid-single-digit growth in 2027 without M&A. The remaining North Dakota Bakken G&P footprint was not addressed.

GS reads management's comments on the MPLX-MPC relationship as a willingness to be flexible in future, not a sign of near-term action. GS sees no meaningful change coming, citing a meaningful cash tax charge if MPC were to roll in MPLX. MPC commercial agreements are up for renewal in early 2028, and both parties intend to renew.

GS keeps a Buy rating and cuts its 12-month price target to $62 from $63, based on an unchanged 11.5x multiple on 2027 EBITDA. The stock closed at $56.55 (9.6% upside), with a distribution yield of about 8% versus a midstream coverage average of about 5%.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $62 from $63 on an unchanged 11.5x multiple on 2027 EBITDA after modest estimate changes and a lower 2027 distribution. Buy rating reiterated with 9.6% upside to the $56.55 close.

sector_views.rationale: MPLX offers one of the highest distribution yields in GS coverage (about 8% vs about 5% midstream average), with growth supported by Permian and Northeast volumes.

earnings_insights: MPLX 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $1,859m (reported 11/5/2026) vs GSe estimate $1,844m and FactSet consensus estimate $1,843m.
3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $1,859m vs 2Q26 reported $1,775m (+5% QoQ) and +5% YoY vs 3Q25 (+7% excluding the Rockies divestiture).
GS estimate for 4Q26 EBITDA: about +2% QoQ, excluding any Titan II contribution.

GS EBITDA estimates (new): 2026E $7,262m, 2027E $7,908m, 2028E $8,308m. Old: $7,251m, $7,891m, $8,295m. Consensus EBITDA: 2026E $7,260m, 2027E $7,789m, 2028E $8,198m. GS estimates exclude the pending divestiture.
risk_factors: Execution on the capital return framework.
Lower than expected Marcellus and Utica growth.
Sooner than expected declines in refined products demand.
Unexpected recontracting headwinds on MPC-facing assets, including Fuels Distribution.
High-multiple acquisitions from third parties or sponsor MPC.
Rates and contract terms could be pressured over time by the combined Northeast upstream customer's greater scale.

tension_points.bull_case: Management still expects 2027 EBITDA growth above 2026 and mid-single-digit growth ahead, with proceeds redeployed into Permian and Marcellus projects. GS says the lower distribution rate more than offsets the lost EBITDA (about $750m saved vs about $500m lost through 2032), and a higher coverage level was likely prudent.
tension_points.bear_case: The asset sale removes about $83m of 2027 EBITDA and cuts the distribution growth outlook to about 8.5% from 12.5%. GS lists execution on the capital return framework as a downside risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The formal 2027 distribution framework, expected alongside 4Q26 results, and the pace of redeploying sale proceeds.

theme_stances.key_argument: The lower distribution rate more than offsets the lost EBITDA from the asset sale, and managing to a higher coverage level was likely prudent.
